title: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review - 2026-03-07 (draft)
content:
SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review - prep notes (draft)
Owner: Ravi Singh
Attendees (planned): Alex Chen, Maya Patel, Jordan Lee, Elena Gomez
Date: 2026-03-07

Purpose: quick status on SLOs, paging trends, follow-ups from last week's incidents, unblock action items before quarterly reliability review. Keep it focused (30-45m).

Agenda (30m)
- 5m: Quick wins / shoutouts
- 10m: SLO health summary + trends (last 7 days)
- 10m: Top incidents & postmortem updates (action tracking)
- 5m: Ops/Rollout concerns (autoscaler / infra changes)
- 5m: Action items / owners / due dates

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Primary serving API availability slipped below target last week (99.87% vs 99.9% target) -> error budget burn ~35% for the 30d window.
- Paging volume increased: avg PD pages/day = 4.2 (week) up from 2.1 (prev week). Two repeat causes: autoscaler flaps and Redis eviction storms.
- Top incidents: SRE-452 (dedicated cluster OOM leading to degraded throughput), SRE-459 (redis eviction cascade -> p95 latency spikes), SRE-461 (scheduled deploy + config drift triggered rollout rollback).

SLOs (user-facing serving API) - last 7 days\- Availability (success rate): 99.87% (target 99.90%)\- Latency p95: 360ms (target 300ms)\- Error rate (5xx): 0.42% (target 0.3%)
Notes: p95 elevated primarily during 03/02 14:10-15:30 window (correlates with SRE-459 redis evictions). Availability drop mostly from two 10-15m incidents and a longer degraded throughput window during autoscaler flaps.

Paging trends / oncall load\- Total PD pages last week: 29\- Avg pages/day: 4.2\- Median time-to-ack: 4m (improved vs 7m previous)\- Most pages were P2/P3; two P1 escalations for degraded throughput.
Root causes observed: autoscaler instability (node churn), redis memory pressure/eviction, one regressional vendor library that increased GC pauses (still investigating PR trace).

Top incidents (short summaries)
1) SRE-452: dedicated cluster OOM (2026-03-02)\- Impact: ~20% throughput degradation for ~40m, some requests retried -> elevated p95\- RCA (working hypothesis): combination of new model variant + lower-than-expected memory headroom on dedicated hosts -> OOM and pod restarts\- Current status: mitigations applied (reverted variant, increased memory requests on canary); full RCA draft in JIRA SRE-452; action items below.

2) SRE-459: redis eviction cascade (2026-03-02 14:05-15:40)\- Impact: p95 latency spike to ~800ms during window; availability hit due to timeouts\- RCA: burst of cache fills after rolling restart + Redis maxmemory misconfig -> eviction thrash. Some clients did not backoff leading to thundering herd\- Fixes applied: increased redis maxmemory, added client-side backoff in SDK patch (PR merged but monitoring), rate-limit on bulk reload job scheduled for next week.

3) SRE-461: deploy rollback due to config drift (2026-03-04)\- Impact: short degraded responses while rollout rolled back (10-12m)\- RCA: canary configuration mismatch (env var difference between canary and prod) -> rollout triggered health checks failures\- Preventative: add canary-to-prod config parity checks in CI (see linked PR).

Action items (tracked)
- Alex Chen: deep-dive autoscaler flaps (logs + metrics) and produce a short runbook for mitigation (node draining, quicker fallback). Due 2026-03-09. Linked to JIRA-SRE-460.
- Maya Patel: finish RCA writeup for SRE-452 (OOM) and propose memory sizing guidelines for model variants. Due 2026-03-10.
- Jordan Lee: validate redis client patch in staging and schedule controlled rollout; add circuit-breaker + backoff defaults to SDK. Due 2026-03-11.
- Elena Gomez: add CI check for canary/prod env var parity and add to rollout gating. Due 2026-03-12.
- Ravi (me): coordinate stakeholder update for product / infra and prepare short note for reliability review deck (metrics + burn rate). Due 2026-03-08.

Discussion points / open questions\- Do we increase availability SLO to 99.95 for certain premium customers? Not for this cycle; need stability first.\- Should we introduce a small safety buffer on memory requests for all model-serving pools? Pros: reduces OOM risk; Cons: increases cost. Need cost estimate from infra.\- Paging fatigue: consider weekly oncall rotation adjustments if pages/day stays >3 for 2 consecutive weeks.

Notes to self / loose ideas\- Track error budget burn by customer tier and route (hosted vs dedicated) -> might need different thresholds\- Create small runbook: \"If autoscaler flaps -> quickly scale to static pool for 30m\" (fast mitigation)\- Consider adding a Redis LRU TTL for bloom/cache objects to avoid full cache reloads after restarts

Links / artifacts\- Full RCA drafts: JIRA-SRE-452, JIRA-SRE-459, JIRA-SRE-461\- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-9876 (weekly reliability dashboard)\- Observability PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/78\- Slack thread: #sre-oncall (thread ts: 1677800000.000400)

Prep for meeting\- Bring the numbers (SLO graph + error budget burn). I will share dashboard link in calendar invite.
\- Ask Alex to show autoscaler logs briefly (5m) and Jordan to confirm redis rollout plan.

Unresolved: need final cost impact estimate for increasing memory buffer on model-serving pools (ask infra team).

End of draft notes.

(Will tidy after sync and convert action items into JIRA tasks / update linked_artifacts.)
